work.title: Water Music, Suite No. 2 in D

version.value: Performing edition not identified. The movement number (12 of the three suites) and the structure heard (39-bar first section played twice, 35-bar middle section, da capo to the Fine at bar 39 without the repeat) match the Hallische Händel-Ausgabe text; no editor or continuo realisation is credited.
version.note: The programme and Commons name the work and movement numbers but no edition. The structure follows from the measured level curve and the Hallische Händel-Ausgabe (Redlich, 1962), which prints a repeat sign after bar 39, the Fine mark at bar 39, and da capo at bar 74. IMSLP’s tally of 74 bars (133 with da capo) does not agree with that reading (74 plus 39 bars of da capo gives 113) and is not used.

value.name: Marine Chamber Orchestra, United States Marine Band

performers.note: Commons gives the conductor as Major Michelle Rakers; the programme prints Major Michelle A. Rakers. No roster of individual players is published in the consulted sources. A trumpet, strings with a double bass, a bassoon and a harpsichord are visible in the Marine Band’s video frames; horns and oboes could not be identified there, though the recording sounds in the bars where the score gives the horns alone.

date.note: Commons gives performance_date 2017-01-29; the programme prints Sunday, January 29, 2017 at 2:00 P.M.; the official video description repeats the date. The Handel group stands after the intermission in the programme. The Commons composition_date field, 1717-07-17, is the date of the documented first performance on the Thames, not a composition date.

place.value: Rachel M. Schlesinger Concert Hall and Arts Center, Northern Virginia Community College, Alexandria Campus, Alexandria, Virginia, United States
place.note: Commons says Schlesinger Concert Hall, Alexandria, VA; the programme gives the full name of the hall and campus.

label.note: No record label is identified. The source is an official concert video on the Marine Band’s YouTube channel; the channel is not treated as a label, and no commercial release was found.

catalogue.note: Born-digital concert video. The YouTube video ID 8Ca_cr54cfM identifies the source video but is not a catalogue number.

matrixTakeSides.note: A concert recording made in digital form has no matrix, take or side numbers.

credits.note: No transfer or mastering engineer is identified. The Commons file history shows the batch upload by the user Mysterymanblue (pattypan), which is an uploader credit, not an engineering credit.

date.note: No transfer date is documented. The YouTube publication date (30 April 2018) and the Commons upload date (28 June 2021) are not session or transfer dates.

processing.value: Opus audio file (48 kHz, two channels, encoder Lavf58.29.100) listed on Commons with the Marine Band’s YouTube playlist as its source; Commons supplies an MP3 access derivative.
processing.note: The file’s own metadata documents the Opus format and encoder. That the audio was taken from the official video’s sound track is inferred from the source field and from the matching title and duration (229 s); the processing chain is not described.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source: Opus

composition.value: Handel (died 1759): the composition is in the public domain.
composition.note: Commons tags the composition PD-old-auto-expired (death year 1759). The performing edition is not identified; editorial copyright in a modern edition, if one was used, is separate from the sound recording.

recording.value: Commons tags the performance and recording PD-USGov-Military-Marines: a work of a United States Marine or employee made as part of official duties, public domain as a work of the U.S. federal government.
recording.note: This is a U.S.-jurisdiction statement, not a claim of worldwide status. The programme carries a general notice that a performance may contain third-party material and should not be assumed to be public domain; no third-party material is identified in this performance of a composition from before 1759, but the notice is recorded here. The official Marine Band YouTube channel published the source video.

rights.creditLine: George Frideric Handel, Water Music, Suite No. 2 in D, HWV 349: II. Alla hornpipe. Marine Chamber Orchestra of the United States Marine Band, Major Michelle Rakers conducting; Rachel M. Schlesinger Concert Hall, Alexandria, Virginia, 29 January 2017. Audio via Wikimedia Commons from the official Marine Band concert video. U.S. federal-government work; public domain in the United States.

sources.title: Händel, Wassermusik Suite II HWV 349, Hallische Händel-Ausgabe IV/13, ed. Hans Ferdinand Redlich (Bärenreiter, 1962), via IMSLP #559922
sources.locator: Printed pp. 44–49 (movement 12, bars 1–74): repeat sign and Fine after bar 39, brass staves resting through bars 40–74, oboes and fagotto resting in bars 67–74, da capo at bar 74. Consulted for bar numbering only; its copyright status in the United States is not established and it is not the stated score source of the orchestra view.

sources.title: Handel, The Celebrated Water-musick in score (London: Samuel Arnold, 1788) — Bibliothèque nationale de France scan on Wikimedia Commons
sources.locator: Printed pp. 39–44 (Commons images 21–24 of 30): the Alla Hornpipe in 3/2 for trumpets, horns, oboes, bassoon, three violin parts, viola and figured bass, with the repeat sign on p. 42 and Da Capo on p. 44. Commons tags the scans PD-old-auto-expired, PD-France and PD-US-expired.
